title: Typeless vs VoiceInk vs Lazur: Choosing the Best Mac Voice Assistant in 2026
metaTitle: Typeless vs VoiceInk: Best Mac Voice Assistant Comparison 2026
description: Comparing Typeless and VoiceInk for Mac dictation and productivity. See how they stack up against Lazur's screen-aware voice assistant features.
intro: Typeless and VoiceInk both aim to speed up your writing on a Mac through voice dictation. Typeless focuses on a broad AI-powered approach to text, while VoiceInk offers a local, open-source model for privacy-conscious users.
tldr: Typeless is a cross-platform tool focused on AI-driven text formatting and language support.
VoiceInk is a local-first, open-source dictation tool for Apple Silicon Macs.
Lazur provides a different approach by acting as a screen-aware assistant that guides you through tasks rather than just typing for you.
Choose Typeless for multi-platform needs, VoiceInk for local privacy, or Lazur if you want an assistant that understands your screen context.

blocks.text: Typeless is built for people who need to handle text across many platforms. It uses AI to fix filler words and format lists automatically. It is a good choice if you work in different environments, including Windows and Linux. The app promotes itself as a way to save time by moving from typing to speaking.

VoiceInk is different. It is built specifically for macOS on Apple Silicon. It uses open-source Whisper models to transcribe your voice locally. This means your data stays on your Mac. It is a one-time purchase, which is rare for software today. It is popular with users who want to avoid subscriptions and cloud-based processing.

Lazur is not just a dictation tool. It sits in your Mac notch and watches your screen when you ask it to. If you hold ⌥ ⌘, you can ask questions about what you see. Lazur can point at buttons, explain steps, or help you find information. It uses your voice to perform everyday Mac tasks like setting reminders or opening apps.

items: Ask Lazur to draw a circle around a button if you are lost.
Hold fn to dictate text into any field on your Mac.
Use Lazur to manage your calendar or music playback.
Research topics using Lazur for Chrome to get summaries.

blocks.text: Privacy is a major concern for voice users. VoiceInk processes audio on your device. It does not send data to the cloud unless you use third-party APIs. This makes it a strong option for sensitive work. Typeless also emphasizes privacy with on-device history storage and no cloud retention.

Lazur handles privacy by only listening and looking at your screen while you hold the shortcut. It does not store your audio or screenshots. It sends data to AI providers only to answer your specific request. The content is never used to train models.

If you need a tool that works on Windows and Linux, Typeless is the clear choice. It is built for cross-platform efficiency. If you want a local-only tool for your M-series Mac and prefer a one-time fee, look at VoiceInk. If you want a Mac-native assistant that can see your screen, point at UI elements, and help you navigate your apps, try Lazur.

faq.question: Can I use VoiceInk on an Intel Mac?
faq.answer: No, VoiceInk requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14.4 or later.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It guides you or points things out so you can do the work.

faq.question: Is Typeless free?
faq.answer: Typeless pricing is not publicly listed on their site. You should check their pricing page for the latest information.
